PTE Essay Topics 2026: 60 Questions

PTE gives you one essay, 20 minutes and 200 to 300 words. The prompts recycle a small number of shapes rather than a fixed list of topics, so the fastest way to prepare is to practise the shapes. Below are 60 practice prompts sorted into the five shapes PTE actually uses, one full model answer, and the trait by trait breakdown that decides your mark.

PTE Write Essay at a glance

Write Essay is the final task of Part 1 Speaking and Writing. You get 20 minutes to plan, write and check a single essay of 200 to 300 words. Pearson scores it against seven traits worth 15 points in total: Content (3), Formal Requirement (2), Development Structure and Coherence (2), Grammar (2), General Linguistic Range (2), Vocabulary Range (2) and Spelling (2).

Why Content is the trait that decides your mark

Content is the only trait worth three points and it is the only trait that can zero the whole essay. An essay that is very short, very long, not in English, or written entirely in capitals scores zero automatically. Answering the question actually asked beats writing beautifully about something adjacent, so spend the first two minutes deciding what the prompt really wants.

The five PTE essay topic types

Pearson describes the prompts as problem and solution statements, arguments for and against a position, and agree or disagree propositions. In practice two more shapes appear often enough to prepare for: advantages and disadvantages, and discuss both views. Each shape wants a different essay skeleton and using the wrong skeleton is the most common way to lose Content marks.

Agree or disagree prompts

Some people believe university education should be free for all citizens. Working from home is more productive than working in an office. Governments should invest in public transport rather than build new roads. Take one clear position and defend it; do not sit on the fence.

Advantages and disadvantages prompts

More and more people are choosing to live alone. Many companies offer unpaid internships. Online learning is replacing classroom teaching at many universities. Give both sides real weight, then say which one is larger and why.

Problem and solution prompts

Traffic congestion is worsening in most large cities. Plastic waste in the oceans continues to increase. Housing has become unaffordable for young people. Answer in two parts: name the causes first, then propose specific measurable actions.

Discuss both views prompts

Some people think exams are the best way to assess students while others prefer continuous assessment. Some argue governments should fund the arts while others say public money should go to essential services. Present both views and then give your own opinion, because omitting the opinion costs Content marks.

A full model answer

The prompt asks whether social media has done more harm than good to society. The model answer opens by taking a clear position, spends one paragraph on the harm, one on the benefit, and a short conclusion that restates which side is heavier. It runs 268 words and uses four linking devices without repeating the same connector.

How PTE Magic scores your essay

The platform returns feedback on grammar, spelling, vocabulary, cohesion and content relevance immediately after submission, mapped to the same traits Pearson uses. That mapping is built from analysis of practice essays written by learners who later sat the real test.

Common mistakes that cost marks

Writing over 300 words, copying phrases from the prompt verbatim, using a memorised template that does not answer the question, and leaving no time to check spelling. Spelling errors are scored twice, once under Spelling and again under Vocabulary Range.

A 20 minute timing plan

Two minutes to analyse the prompt and choose a position. Three minutes to outline three paragraphs. Twelve minutes to write. Three minutes to check spelling, subject verb agreement and word count. Practising this split is worth more than learning another template.

Where to practise next

Start with the agree or disagree shape because it is the most common, then move to discuss both views which learners find hardest. Full length mock tests on the platform time all four skills in sequence so the essay does not feel isolated.

Essay requirements for Canada

Learners applying to Canada should confirm the score their institution or visa category requires before booking, because requirements differ by programme.
